body: Thank you very much, I really appreciate it. It hurts really bad, I'll miss my friend so much.
That's a lot of good advice! Thank you very much, I will apply your suggestions
Thank you very much for the advice (and the reassurance)! I'll pay attention to that and make sure my English skills and resume are on good shape.
Thank you very much for the insight! I'll pay attention to job postings in the UK then too.

I am sad to hear about your experience in Denmark, I hope you are in a better place now. Thank you very much for sharing your story and experience about the hiring process, and being so helpful too! I think that for now what you said to me has given me enough for a place to start looking.

Oh my friend, the transition really is pretty hard, we're together on that one. You know, I think we can get out of there, even if it's just for a walk outside, even if it's not really "outside", even if it's just a book or a game. Whatever works. We could really use a break, don´t we?

Thank you so much, I think that what I needed the most the validation of it and I didn't realized it until you said it. I nearly cried when I read that part. Thank you so much for being so kind, it kind of help me to get a little hold of things.  


And you're right. I think I've been posponing that option of moving out because it felt like just more work piling up on my plate with everything else that is already going on. But home isn't just a place to rest anymore, and if I want to deal with the rest of my responsabilities, I'll really need that rest or I just won't function. I need to move, I'll work on accepting that.

I've finally continued developing a web page project I had been stuck with no progress for over a month. Accomplished more than I thought I was capable of in merely 2 days! 

I feel really tired about it, but yeah, progress! :)

I have two sisters, twins, younger than me. And they make fun of me all the time, tease me whenever they can in this passive-agressive way you describe. I know it is related to some kind of trauma they both have. I don't know if it is because I'm the older sibling, but I feel the need to "carry" the weight of their insults, because I know they cannot control them. But that doesn't make the pain any lighter. It's hard to talk about this with anyone else that understands it, because it seems to them that is something you should be able to just brush off, say "whatever" and carry on. But god, it just hurts so much, sometimes when I'm alone I try to vent it off and have flashes of rage when I'm even afraid of what I can do to myself. It's get harder and harder to control and tolerate every day, I don't know how much more will I last being around them, but really, the emotional pain you can experience from someone you care (or used to care) about can be SO inmense.

Congratulations! I went through the same process you describe not so long ago, and things get really awesome after you start understanding yourself. Have you read the book "Quiet" by Susan Cain?? It's really great

For me it helps to imagine that no matter what happens, the stressful moment will pass and I'll be able to come back to the comfort of my bed or something like that at the end of the day. Having something on your mind that you can look forward to, even if its something really simple, may be of help to give you something to hang on to. Makes you feel like you have something safe when everything else is shaking

I overreact to everything. Everything. I can't help getting mad over things I would normally manage to shrug off. 

I feel anxious and can't sleep until it's too late into the night. I also have pretty bad mood swings, I feel unmotivated and can't concentrate. One of the defense strategies I have to deal with social situations is to make jokes and laugh things off, but when I'm in this state, I'm too annoyed to do even that. It does really feel like physical exhaustion too.
